findings.title: Bee Stealer Targets Codex And Claude, Uses AI To Profile Victims
findings.summary_md: BlackFog reported Bee Stealer version 2.1 with an AI PC profile feature that sends a significant portion of each stolen log to a neural network and writes the result to ProfileEn.txt and ProfileRu.txt in English and Russian. In a controlled test, the files were produced but could not identify the owner because the test machine had little browser data, which the researchers read as evidence that processing happens after exfiltration. They also found dedicated .codex and .claude collection paths in a builder-generated sample, and noted that the operator panel supports filtering, full-text search, bulk log downloads and a Google token tool. The authors argue that such profiles accelerate victim selection before sessions expire or defenders respond.

findings.title: The rise of AI-powered infostealers: threat actors automate victim profiling
findings.summary_md: BI.ZONE described two infostealer listings, the Windows-based Bee Stealer and the macOS malware agent AVENGER, that automatically profile compromised systems with a language model. For Bee Stealer, a large part of the stolen log is processed on the attacker control panel and the output fills fields for likely profession, interests, frequent sites and the purpose of key domains; AVENGER uses browser and command history, messages, email and configuration files to identify workplace, banks and digital assets. The team said profile generation speeds triage of large log sets and lets sellers sort logs as developer or financial access before sessions expire. It expects future malware to move from passive profiling to automated monetization choices such as session hijacking, cloud logins and spearphishing.
